newsitem.title: USA: Albany County Airport, N.Y., to sell bonds - paper.
newsitem.headline: Albany County Airport, N.Y., to sell bonds - paper.

text.p: The Albany County Airport Authority's plans to sell as much as $100 million of bonds next month for a $158 million expansion got a boost when a committee gave its approval to modifying a lease in favor of the bondholders, the Albany Times Union said on Tuesday.

A committee of county legislators offered to back the bonds with airport revenues in case of a default, a plan that could save the airport up to $9.8 million by lowering interest costs, the paper said.

The lease, which had required airport revenues to be paid to the county before bondholders, would be altered so that if the airport authority defaults, the county would let the airport revenues, from airline fees, store rentals and parking lot charges, to be used to repay the bonds.
The airport's chief fiscal officer told the paper that modifying the lease should lower the interest rates the new bonds fetch to as low as 5.9 percent.
But the change still needs approval by the full legislature, which is expected to vote on Monday.

The paper said that the authority hired Lehman Brothers to head a six-firm underwriting team that includes First Albany Corp, Pryor, McClendon, Counts & Co., M.R. Beal & Co., J.P. Morgan Securities, and PaineWebber.
